a.note: Configuration cell. a is the dimensionless return-period exponent in the local IDF relation. Use coefficients fitted for the study location.

ADD.note: Configuration cell. ADD is antecedent dry days. When no initial-buildup raster is used, it enters the exponential buildup initialization B0 = C1 [1 - exp(-C2 ADD)].

Albedo_path.note: Configuration cell. Albedo_path is an optional raster of surface albedo from 0 to 1. It is used only when spatial albedo is enabled for the energy-balance evapotranspiration calculation.

alfa_1.note: Configuration cell. alfa_1 is the coefficient in the derived channel-depth relation H = alfa_1 A^alfa_2, where A is contributing area in km2. It is used only when channel geometry is derived rather than supplied as rasters.

alfa_2.note: Configuration cell. alfa_2 is the exponent in the derived channel-depth relation H = alfa_1 A^alfa_2. Use a value calibrated or justified for the target river network.

alfa_max.note: Configuration cell. alfa_max is the upper adaptive-timestep coefficient retained for compatible time-control configurations. Keep it positive and no smaller than alfa_min; current routing stability calculations use alfa_min for the conservative candidate step.

alfa_min.note: Configuration cell. alfa_min is the lower Courant safety coefficient used when HydroPol2D calculates a stable surface-routing timestep. Smaller values are more conservative and usually increase runtime.

AlphaVG_path.note: Configuration cell. AlphaVG_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the soil van Genuchten alpha in 1/m. It overrides the SOIL_parameters value of each class where finite (nodata keeps the class value).

b.note: Configuration cell. b is the duration offset in the local IDF relation, expressed in minutes when duration is entered in minutes.

B1_path.note: Configuration cell. B1_path is an optional GeoTIFF path for the spatial C1 buildup asymptote. It is read only when water quality and raster water-quality inputs are enabled; use values and units consistent with the LULC C1 parameter.

B2_path.note: Configuration cell. B2_path is an optional GeoTIFF path for the spatial C2 buildup-rate parameter. It is read only when water quality and raster water-quality inputs are enabled.

beta_1.note: Configuration cell. beta_1 is the coefficient in the derived channel-width relation W = beta_1 A^beta_2, where A is contributing area in km2. It is bypassed by supplied river-width rasters.

beta_2.note: Configuration cell. beta_2 is the exponent in the derived channel-width relation W = beta_1 A^beta_2. It controls how quickly generated channels widen downstream.

Bmax.note: Configuration cell. Bmax is the upper pollutant buildup bound in g/m2 used by the selected buildup/washoff formulation. It limits physically stored pollutant mass where that option is active.

Bmin.note: Configuration cell. Bmin is the lower pollutant buildup bound in g/m2 used by the selected buildup/washoff formulation. Use a nonnegative value no larger than Bmax.

c.note: Configuration cell. c is the dimensionless duration exponent in the local IDF relation. It controls how intensity decays as storm duration increases.

capillary_field_capacity_head_m.note: Configuration cell. capillary_field_capacity_head_m is the suction head in metres that defines field capacity: the water a layer keeps after the water table falls out of it. Specific yield = theta_s minus theta at this head, and capillary rise from the water table refills a layer only up to this water content. Default 3.3 m (about 33 kPa). Lower it to represent a capillary fringe above shallow water tables (specific yield falls with it).

date_begin.note: Configuration cell. date_begin is the simulation start datetime. Use the same time reference as rainfall, evapotranspiration, inflow, stage, and observation time series.

date_end.note: Configuration cell. date_end is the simulation end datetime. It must be later than date_begin; forcing values outside this interval are not part of the run.

deep_aquifer_initial_baseflow_mm_day.note: Configuration cell. deep_aquifer_initial_baseflow_mm_day is the deep-aquifer baseflow per unit area on the start date, in mm/day (option 1: from a gauge, e.g. hydropol2d estimate-deep-baseflow, which divides the deep part of the start-date baseflow by the drainage area). Each subbasin starts at storage S0 = q0 x subbasin area x deep_aquifer_tau_days. Leave empty to start empty. Set this or deep_aquifer_mean_recharge_mm_year, not both.

deep_aquifer_mean_recharge_mm_year.unit: mm/year; steady state, q0 = f x R
deep_aquifer_mean_recharge_mm_year.note: Configuration cell. deep_aquifer_mean_recharge_mm_year is the long-term mean recharge to the water table, in mm/year (option 2: no gauge needed). The deep aquifer starts at steady state: q0 = deep_recharge_fraction x this recharge, and S0 = q0 x subbasin area x deep_aquifer_tau_days. Set this or deep_aquifer_initial_baseflow_mm_day, not both.

deep_recharge_fraction.note: Configuration cell. deep_recharge_fraction is the share, in (0, 1], of water-table recharge sent to the deep aquifer: a slow linear reservoir per subbasin below the 2-D groundwater model. The rest recharges the shallow aquifer. Read only when flag_deep_aquifer = 1.

DeepAquiferChannelWeight_path.note: Configuration cell. DeepAquiferChannelWeight_path is a GeoTIFF of non-negative weights saying where each subbasin's deep-aquifer outflow returns to the surface, e.g. 1 on river cells and 0 elsewhere. Weights are normalized within each subbasin, which needs at least one positive weight. Required only when flag_deep_aquifer = 1.

DeepAquiferInitialState_path.note: Configuration cell. DeepAquiferInitialState_path is an optional JSON file with the starting storage of each deep-aquifer subbasin (the Builder's DeepAquiferInitialState.json from the recession calibration). Use it instead of the two Deep Aquifer Initial State values, not together with them.

DeepAquiferSubbasins_path.note: Configuration cell. DeepAquiferSubbasins_path is an integer GeoTIFF of subbasin IDs (1, 2, ...). Each ID is one deep-aquifer reservoir. Required only when flag_deep_aquifer = 1; every active cell needs a positive ID. A raster of all 1s gives one reservoir for the whole domain.

DEM_path.note: Configuration cell. DEM_path is the required path to the terrain elevation GeoTIFF, with elevations in metres. It defines the model domain, grid geometry, and topographic gradients.

depth_wse.note: Configuration cell. depth_wse is the minimum water depth in metres used when water-surface-elevation maps are produced. It avoids reporting water-surface elevation where the cell is effectively dry.

dt_design.note: Configuration cell. dt_design is the time increment in minutes used to discretize the generated design hyetograph. It should be short enough to resolve the intended rainfall peak.

DTB_path.note: Configuration cell. DTB_path is an optional DEPTH-TO-BEDROCK GeoTIFF in metres below the land surface. Legacy groundwater: it is the soil depth, and the aquifer lives inside it. Layered subsurface: it is the bottom of the whole column (soil plus weathered rock); the soil thickness is set separately by subsurface_soil_base_depth_m or SoilBaseDepth_path. Required for legacy groundwater; optional with flag_layered_subsurface = 1, where an empty DTB_path falls back to subsurface_depth_to_bedrock_m, then to the DTB (m) of each soil class in SOIL_parameters.xlsx.

feddes_h1_m.note: Configuration cell. feddes_h1_m is the anaerobiosis head in metres (negative). Wetter than h1, roots take no water (no oxygen). Default -0.1 m.

feddes_h2_m.note: Configuration cell. feddes_h2_m is the head in metres (negative) where uptake becomes optimal. Between h1 and h2 the stress factor rises from 0 to 1. Default -0.25 m.

feddes_h3_high_m.note: Configuration cell. feddes_h3_high_m is h3 at high transpiration demand (potential ET of 5 mm/d or more), in metres (negative); usually less negative than feddes_h3_low_m, so stress starts earlier on high-demand days. Leave it empty to use feddes_h3_m.

feddes_h3_low_m.note: Configuration cell. feddes_h3_low_m is h3 at low transpiration demand (potential ET of 1 mm/d or less), in metres (negative). With feddes_h3_high_m, h3 is interpolated by demand as in SWAP. Leave it empty to use feddes_h3_m.

feddes_h3_m.note: Configuration cell. feddes_h3_m is the head in metres (negative) where water stress starts. Between h3 and h4 the factor falls from 1 to 0. Used when feddes_h3_low_m and feddes_h3_high_m are empty. Default -4 m.

feddes_h4_m.note: Configuration cell. feddes_h4_m is the wilting-point head in metres (negative). Drier than h4, roots take no water. Default -80 m (-0.8 MPa).

flag_wse.note: Configuration cell. flag_wse controls water-surface-elevation map output: 0 disables it and 1 enables it. The map uses DEM elevation plus simulated water depth where depth exceeds depth_wse.

groundwater_courant.note: Configuration cell. groundwater_courant is the dimensionless safety factor used to limit the Boussinesq groundwater timestep. Use a value greater than zero and no greater than one; smaller values improve stability at the cost of more updates.

groundwater_min_dt_s.note: Configuration cell. groundwater_min_dt_s is the shortest interval in seconds allowed between lateral groundwater updates, even when the stability limit asks for less. Default 60 s.

groundwater_target_dt_s.note: Configuration cell. groundwater_target_dt_s is the interval in seconds between lateral groundwater updates in the layered scheme. A shorter interval is used when the stability limit requires it. Vertical soil fluxes still run every model timestep. Default 3600 s.

GroundwaterKsat_path.note: Configuration cell. GroundwaterKsat_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the aquifer horizontal conductivity kgsat in mm/h. It overrides the SOIL_parameters kgsat of each class where finite. Layered subsurface: it is the rock Kh fallback when regolith_ksat_h_mm_h and RegolithKsatH_path are empty.

GW_Dirichlet_Head_path.note: Configuration cell. GW_Dirichlet_Head_path is an optional prescribed groundwater-head elevation GeoTIFF in metres. Finite raster cells define the groundwater Dirichlet boundary; no-data cells remain unconstrained.

GW_table_path.note: Configuration cell. GW_table_path is an optional initial groundwater-table elevation GeoTIFF in metres, using the same vertical datum as the DEM. It is read when groundwater or baseflow is enabled and is constrained below the land surface.

ImperviousFraction_path.note: Configuration cell. ImperviousFraction_path is an optional raster of fractional impervious cover from 0 to 1. It refines infiltration behavior within a cell; values outside this range are not physically meaningful.

Initial_Buildup_path.note: Configuration cell. Initial_Buildup_path is an optional pollutant-mass GeoTIFF in kg per cell. It is read only when flag_initial_buildup and the water-quality module are enabled.

Initial_Snow_Depth_path.note: Configuration cell. Initial_Snow_Depth_path is an optional initial snow-depth GeoTIFF in mm. It is read only when snow modeling is enabled; when paired with SWE, the model checks their physical consistency and derives density.

Initial_Soil_Moisture_path.note: Configuration cell. Initial_Soil_Moisture_path is an optional initial soil-water-storage GeoTIFF. Despite its legacy name, values are interpreted as storage above residual moisture in mm, not as volumetric water content; it is read with flag_warmup.

Initial_SWE_path.note: Configuration cell. Initial_SWE_path is an optional initial snow-water-equivalent GeoTIFF in mm water equivalent. It is read only when snow modeling is enabled; negative values are invalid and no-data cells use the default zero-snow condition.

K.note: Configuration cell. K is the scale coefficient of the local IDF relation i = K RP^a / (b + duration)^c. Its units must be consistent with intensity in mm/h and duration in minutes.

K_value.note: Configuration cell. K_value is the smoothing strength passed to the constrained regularized stream-profile smoother. It is used only when DEM smoothing is enabled; larger values produce stronger profile regularization.

KsatNearSurface_path.note: Configuration cell. KsatNearSurface_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the saturated hydraulic conductivity of the near-surface soil layer in mm/h. It overrides ksat x Ks_multiplier_near_surface of each SOIL class where finite (nodata keeps the class value).

KsatRootZone_path.note: Configuration cell. KsatRootZone_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the saturated hydraulic conductivity of the root-zone soil layer in mm/h. It overrides ksat x Ks_multiplier_root_zone of each SOIL class where finite (nodata keeps the class value).

KsatTransmission_path.note: Configuration cell. KsatTransmission_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the saturated hydraulic conductivity of the transmission soil layer in mm/h. It overrides ksat x Ks_multiplier_transmission of each SOIL class where finite (nodata keeps the class value).

LAI_path.note: Configuration cell. LAI_path is an optional leaf-area-index raster in m2 leaf area per m2 ground area. It is used by canopy interception and vegetation-related evapotranspiration when the relevant flags are enabled.

LULC_path.note: Configuration cell. LULC_path is the required categorical land-use/land-cover GeoTIFF. Raster class codes are matched to LULC_parameters.xlsx; unmapped codes receive the documented area-weighted fallback.

Manning.note: Configuration cell. Manning is the in-bank channel Manning roughness in s m^-1/3, applied on river cells. Land and overbank cells use the LULC_parameters.xlsx roughness.

max_time_step.note: Configuration cell. max_time_step is the largest allowable surface-routing timestep in seconds. It limits the timestep during slowly varying periods and should be greater than or equal to min_time_step.

min_area.note: Configuration cell. min_area is the contributing-area threshold in km2 used to extract the modeled stream network and derive hydraulic geometry from flow accumulation.

min_Bt.note: Configuration cell. min_Bt is the minimum pollutant surface mass density in g/m2 retained by the water-quality washoff calculation. It prevents numerical treatment of negligible pollutant mass.

min_time_step.note: Configuration cell. min_time_step is the smallest allowable surface-routing timestep in seconds. Use a positive value small enough to resolve rapid wetting, shallow flow, and steep terrain.

NVG_path.note: Configuration cell. NVG_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the soil van Genuchten n (greater than 1, dimensionless). It overrides the SOIL_parameters value of each class where finite (nodata keeps the class value).

Pol_min.note: Configuration cell. Pol_min is the minimum pollutant concentration in mg/L displayed in water-quality maps. It is a visualization threshold; values below it are hidden in plots but are not removed from the mass balance.

Rainfall Duration.note: Configuration cell. Rainfall Duration is the total design-storm duration in minutes. It sets the length of the generated Alternated Blocks or Huff hyetograph.

record_time_hydrographs.note: Configuration cell. record_time_hydrographs is the interval in minutes between saved outlet, inflow, and gauge hydrograph records. Choose an interval that resolves the expected hydrograph response.

record_time_maps.note: Configuration cell. record_time_maps is the interval in minutes between saved spatial model maps. A shorter interval increases output detail and disk use without changing the simulation physics.

record_time_spatial_ETP.note: Configuration cell. record_time_spatial_ETP is the interval in minutes between saved spatial evaporation and transpiration products. Shorter intervals produce more detailed files and increase storage demand.

record_time_spatial_rainfall.note: Configuration cell. record_time_spatial_rainfall is the interval in minutes used to save or aggregate spatial rainfall information. For raster rainfall, it should be compatible with the map-output interval.

regolith_alpha_vg_m_inverse.note: Configuration cell. regolith_alpha_vg_m_inverse is the van Genuchten alpha of the rock layers, in 1/m. With regolith_n_vg it sets how much water the rock keeps after draining, and so its specific yield. RegolithAlphaVG_path overrides it cell by cell. Default 2.

regolith_ksat_h_mm_h.note: Configuration cell. regolith_ksat_h_mm_h is the horizontal saturated hydraulic conductivity of the rock layers in mm/h, used for lateral groundwater flow. Leave it empty to use the groundwater Ksat (kgsat) of SOIL_parameters.xlsx. RegolithKsatH_path overrides it cell by cell.

regolith_ksat_v_mm_h.note: Configuration cell. regolith_ksat_v_mm_h is the vertical saturated hydraulic conductivity of the rock layers in mm/h. It limits drainage and recharge through the rock. RegolithKsatV_path overrides it cell by cell. Default 5 mm/h.

regolith_lateral_conductivity_multiplier.note: Configuration cell. regolith_lateral_conductivity_multiplier scales the horizontal conductivity of the rock layers below the soil base (regolith_ksat_h_mm_h, RegolithKsatH_path or kgsat). Fitted by the layered groundwater recession calibration (low flows drain through the rock); 1 keeps the mapped values.

regolith_n_vg.note: Configuration cell. regolith_n_vg is the van Genuchten n of the rock layers (dimensionless, greater than 1). RegolithNVG_path overrides it cell by cell. Default 1.5.

regolith_specific_yield.note: Configuration cell. regolith_specific_yield is the drainable porosity of the rock layers (dimensionless). Leave it empty to derive it from the van Genuchten values as theta_s minus the water content at field capacity. A value here or RegolithSpecificYield_path overrides that; it must not exceed theta_s minus theta_r.

regolith_theta_r.note: Configuration cell. regolith_theta_r is the residual water content of the rock layers, in m3/m3, below regolith_theta_s. RegolithThetaR_path overrides it cell by cell. Default 0.05.

regolith_theta_s.note: Configuration cell. regolith_theta_s is the saturated water content (porosity) of the rock layers below the soil base, in m3/m3. RegolithThetaS_path overrides it cell by cell. Default 0.35.

RegolithAlphaVG_path.note: Configuration cell. RegolithAlphaVG_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the rock-layer van Genuchten alpha in 1/m. It overrides regolith_alpha_vg_m_inverse where finite. Layered subsurface only.

RegolithKsatH_path.note: Configuration cell. RegolithKsatH_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the rock-layer horizontal saturated conductivity in mm/h, used for lateral groundwater flow. It overrides regolith_ksat_h_mm_h where finite. Layered subsurface only. Global source: GLHYMPS 2.0 permeability.

RegolithKsatV_path.note: Configuration cell. RegolithKsatV_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the rock-layer vertical saturated conductivity in mm/h. It overrides regolith_ksat_v_mm_h where finite. Layered subsurface only.

RegolithNVG_path.note: Configuration cell. RegolithNVG_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the rock-layer van Genuchten n. It overrides regolith_n_vg where finite. Layered subsurface only.

RegolithSpecificYield_path.note: Configuration cell. RegolithSpecificYield_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the rock-layer specific yield. It overrides the derived value (theta_s minus field capacity) where finite. Layered subsurface only.

RegolithThetaR_path.note: Configuration cell. RegolithThetaR_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the rock-layer residual water content in m3/m3. It overrides regolith_theta_r where finite. Layered subsurface only.

RegolithThetaS_path.note: Configuration cell. RegolithThetaS_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the rock-layer saturated water content in m3/m3. It overrides regolith_theta_s where finite. Layered subsurface only.

resolution_resample.note: Configuration cell. resolution_resample is the working model-grid resolution in metres when raster resampling is enabled. All model inputs are aligned to this resolution during preprocessing.

RiverDepths_path.note: Configuration cell. RiverDepths_path is an optional river-depth GeoTIFF in metres. It is paired with RiverWidths_path for the active embedded-channel model and must be positive where a channel is present.

RiverWidths_path.note: Configuration cell. RiverWidths_path is an optional river-width GeoTIFF in metres. It is required for the active Neal (2012) embedded-channel model when flag_subgrid and flag_river_rasters are enabled; valid embedded widths must remain smaller than the coarse-cell size.

RP.note: Configuration cell. RP is the design-storm return period in years. It is used by the selected IDF relation to calculate rainfall intensity.

sl.note: Configuration cell. sl is the minimum imposed drainage gradient in m/m used by terrain conditioning when minimum-slope imposition is enabled.

slope_DTM.note: Configuration cell. slope_DTM is the slope threshold in percent used by the DTM filter. It is read only when the DTM filtering option is enabled.

slope_outlet.note: Configuration cell. slope_outlet is the positive normal-flow energy slope in m/m applied at configured outlet cells. It should represent the downstream channel or terrain gradient beyond the modeled domain.

soil_lateral_anisotropy.note: Configuration cell. soil_lateral_anisotropy is the horizontal-to-vertical conductivity ratio of the three soil layers: Kh = anisotropy x Ksat. 1 means isotropic. Default 1.

soil_lateral_conductivity_multiplier.note: Configuration cell. soil_lateral_conductivity_multiplier scales the horizontal conductivity of the three soil layers (soil Ksat x soil_lateral_anisotropy) for lateral groundwater flow. Vertical Ksat and infiltration do not change. Fitted by the layered groundwater recession calibration (high flows drain through the soil); 1 keeps the mapped values.

SOIL_path.note: Configuration cell. SOIL_path is the required categorical soil-class GeoTIFF. Raster class codes are matched to SOIL_parameters.xlsx; unmapped codes receive the documented area-weighted fallback.

SoilBaseDepth_path.note: Configuration cell. SoilBaseDepth_path is an optional GeoTIFF of SOIL THICKNESS in metres below ground (the soil base). It overrides subsurface_soil_base_depth_m where finite. Layered subsurface only. Global source: SoilGrids BDRICM.

SpecificYield_path.note: Configuration cell. SpecificYield_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the aquifer specific yield Sy (dimensionless) for the legacy groundwater scheme. It overrides the SOIL_parameters Sy of each class where finite. Not used by the layered subsurface, where Sy comes from the retention curves (or regolith_specific_yield).

subsurface_deep_first_thickness_m.note: Configuration cell. subsurface_deep_first_thickness_m is the thickness in metres of the first rock layer directly below the soil base. Each next layer is subsurface_deep_growth_ratio times thicker, up to subsurface_deep_max_thickness_m. Default 0.25 m.

subsurface_deep_growth_ratio.note: Configuration cell. subsurface_deep_growth_ratio multiplies each rock layer's thickness to get the next one: 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 4, ... m with the defaults. Use a value of at least 1. Default 2.

subsurface_deep_max_thickness_m.note: Configuration cell. subsurface_deep_max_thickness_m is the largest rock-layer thickness in metres. Layers keep this thickness down to the column bottom. Default 4 m.

subsurface_depth_to_bedrock_m.unit: m; after DTB_path, before SOIL DTB (m)
subsurface_depth_to_bedrock_m.note: Configuration cell. subsurface_depth_to_bedrock_m is the DEPTH TO BEDROCK in metres below ground: the bottom of the whole modelled column, soil plus the weathered rock below it. It is deeper than (or equal to) the soil thickness. Priority: DTB_path raster, then this value, then the DTB (m) of each soil class in SOIL_parameters.xlsx, with a warning. Capped at subsurface_max_depth_m.

subsurface_drainage_substeps.note: Configuration cell. subsurface_drainage_substeps is the number of sub-steps for gravity drainage between layers inside one model timestep. 1 is enough for most cases; raise it (2 to 10) for thin, highly conductive layers. Default 1.

subsurface_max_depth_m.note: Configuration cell. subsurface_max_depth_m caps the modelled column in metres below ground: column bottom = min(depth to bedrock, this value). Default 50 m.

subsurface_soil_base_depth_m.note: Configuration cell. subsurface_soil_base_depth_m is the SOIL THICKNESS in metres below ground: where the soil ends and weathered rock (regolith) begins. The three soil layers (near-surface, root zone, transmission) use SOIL_parameters.xlsx down to this depth. SoilBaseDepth_path overrides it cell by cell. It is capped at the depth to bedrock. Default 2.0 m.

tau.note: Configuration cell. tau is the dimensionless regularization setting passed to the constrained regularized stream-profile smoother. It is used only when DEM smoothing is enabled.

ThetaR_path.note: Configuration cell. ThetaR_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the soil residual water content theta_r in m3/m3. It overrides the SOIL_parameters value of each class where finite (nodata keeps the class value).

ThetaS_path.note: Configuration cell. ThetaS_path is an optional GeoTIFF of the soil saturated water content theta_s in m3/m3. It overrides the SOIL_parameters value of each class where finite (nodata keeps the class value), for all soil layers.

time_save_ETP.note: Configuration cell. time_save_ETP is the interval in minutes used for evapotranspiration-product saving and related time-series bookkeeping. It affects output timing, not the evapotranspiration calculation itself.

time_step_change.note: Configuration cell. time_step_change is the positive time increment in seconds used for timestep-refresh bookkeeping and diagnostic alignment. It is not the groundwater update interval.

time_step_model.note: Configuration cell. time_step_model is the nominal surface-model timestep in seconds. It initializes the routing loop; adaptive timestepping may replace it with a stable value between min_time_step and max_time_step.

W1_path.note: Configuration cell. W1_path is an optional GeoTIFF path for the spatial C3 washoff coefficient. It is read only when water quality and raster water-quality inputs are enabled.

W2_path.note: Configuration cell. W2_path is an optional GeoTIFF path for the spatial C4 washoff exponent. It is read only when water quality and raster water-quality inputs are enabled.

Warmup_Depth_path.note: Configuration cell. Warmup_Depth_path is an optional initial surface-water-depth GeoTIFF in metres. It is read only when flag_warmup is enabled and initializes surface storage before routing.

flag_rainfall.note:
Enables rainfall forcing. Use this with one selected rainfall source: a lumped time series, gauge interpolation, a scheduled raster sequence, or a satellite product.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_timestep.note:
Selects the full timestep-stability treatment for supported routing solvers. Use the validated default unless testing a specific numerical formulation.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_GPU.note:
Runs supported arrays and calculations on a compatible MATLAB GPU. Leave disabled when a compatible GPU is not available.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_warmup.note:
Initializes the simulation from the configured warm-up state rather than the standard initial-state rasters.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_resample.note:
Resamples ancillary rasters to the DEM grid during preprocessing when their grid differs from the DEM.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_export_maps.note:
Exports scheduled spatial model outputs such as flood depth and related maps.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_spatial_rainfall.note:
Interpolates rainfall from the configured rainfall gauges to every model cell. Gauge coordinates and a common rainfall time series are required.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_infiltration.note:
Enables infiltration and the layered soil-water balance. Disabling it also disables evapotranspiration in the current model.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_single.note:
Stores supported numerical arrays in single precision to reduce memory use. Keep disabled when maximum numerical precision is required.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_initial_buildup.note:
Initializes water-quality buildup using the configured antecedent dry-period and buildup settings.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_smoothening.note:
Applies constrained stream-profile smoothing during DEM preprocessing. This option requires Optimization Toolbox.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_river_heigth_compensation.note:
Applies the legacy river-height compensation adjustment where the case configuration supports it.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_ETP.note:
Enables evapotranspiration. HydroPol2D uses the configured meteorological or map inputs to calculate evaporation and transpiration.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_critical.note:
Uses the critical-flow outlet treatment where the selected routing solver supports it. This is distinct from the normal-flow outlet selected with flag_outlet_type.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_trunk.note:
Uses the trunk-stream processing option during terrain and drainage-network preparation.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_dashboard.note:
Creates the configured dashboard-oriented outputs during the simulation.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_input_rainfall_map.note:
Reads a time-indexed sequence of rainfall rasters from the Satellite or Radar Rainfall table in General_Data. Do not enable this together with another spatial-rainfall source.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_D8.note:
Enables D8 terrain-routing and drainage preprocessing where applicable. Local-inertial routing itself remains face based.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_fill_DEM.note:
Fills terrain depressions before deriving drainage directions and flow accumulation.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_elapsed_time.note:
Prints or records elapsed computational time for the simulation.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_rainfall_multiple_runs.note:
Activates the legacy multiple-rainfall-run workflow. Leave disabled for one standard rainfall event.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_CA.note:
Selects the cellular-automata hydrodynamic routing option. Do not enable it together with local inertial or full momentum routing.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_smooth_cells.note:
Applies the configured cell-level DEM smoothing treatment during preprocessing.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_obs_gauges.note:
Exports modeled values at the observation-gauge coordinates listed in General_Data.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_data_source.note:
Selects the legacy rainfall-data source pathway. Leave disabled unless a case was prepared specifically for that workflow.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_inertial.note:
Selects the local-inertial hydrodynamic solver. It is the required routing solver for the active Neal (2012) channel-subgrid extension.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_reduce_DEM.note:
Applies the configured river-channel DEM reduction during preprocessing.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_export_groundwater_maps.note:
Exports scheduled groundwater water-table-depth rasters when groundwater modelling is enabled.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_inflow.note:
Applies one or more prescribed discharge hydrographs at the inlet coordinates defined in Inflow_Hydrograph.xlsx.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_waterbalance.note:
Writes water-balance diagnostics during the run. Enable this for validation and for routine model checks.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_satellite_rainfall.note:
Activates the satellite-rainfall forcing workflow. It prepares an hourly spatial-rainfall schedule and enables rainfall automatically.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_waterquality.note:
Enables pollutant buildup, washoff, transport, and output calculations.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_alternated_blocks.note:
Generates the configured alternating-block design storm instead of reading a rainfall time series.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_reservoir.note:
Enables the reservoir and control-structure module using the configured reservoir inputs.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_huff.note:
Generates the configured Huff design storm instead of reading a rainfall time series.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_wq_model.note:
Selects the water-quality formulation. Value 0 uses the mass-based buildup/washoff mode; use other values only for supported legacy configurations.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_stage_hydrograph.note:
Applies a prescribed water-level hydrograph at the configured stage-boundary location(s).

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_groundwater_modeling.note:
Enables the coupled layered-soil recharge and saturated groundwater module.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_input_ETP_map.note:
Reads paired transpiration and evaporation raster schedules from General_Data. Both schedules must have the same time entries.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_real_time_satellite_rainfall.note:
Activates the real-time satellite rainfall workflow. This experimental option creates a short rolling spatial-rainfall schedule.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_dam_break.note:
Activates the dam-break forcing workflow for cases configured with dam-break inputs.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_human_instability.note:
Calculates depth-velocity human-instability indicators. Value 0 disables it; value 1 uses the basic classification and value 3 enables the extended classification.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_boundary.note:
Activates the configured open/perimeter boundary treatment. Define the outlet mask and outlet slope carefully because this setting controls water removal at the domain edge.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_numerical_scheme.note:
Chooses the local-inertial discretization: 1 = Bates, 2 = slope-upwind, 3 = slope-centered. The value is used only by routing options that call the inertial scheme.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_outlet_type.note:
Chooses the outlet relation: 1 = normal-flow outlet using slope_outlet; 2 = critical-flow outlet. The selected outlet cells determine where this relation is applied.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_adaptive_timestepping.note:
Updates the surface-routing timestep from the stability limits during the simulation. Keep enabled for most dynamic simulations.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_neglect_infiltration_river.note:
Sets infiltration and initial abstraction to zero in identified river cells.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_neal_channel.note:
Activates the Neal (2012) embedded rectangular channel and floodplain extension. It requires flag_inertial = 1, structured raster topology, and valid river-width and river-depth rasters.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_spatial_albedo.note:
Uses the supplied albedo raster instead of the scalar default albedo.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_river_rasters.note:
Uses supplied RiverWidths and RiverDepths rasters to define the channel geometry for the active subgrid model.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_baseflow.note:
Enables the configured baseflow contribution where the selected hydrologic workflow supports it.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_kinematic.note:
Selects the kinematic-wave routing alternative. Do not combine it with local inertial, full momentum, or cellular automata routing.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_diffusive.note:
Selects the diffusive-wave routing alternative. Do not combine it with local inertial, full momentum, or cellular automata routing.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_DTM.note:
Uses the DTM-processing pathway for terrain preparation when that workflow is required by the input data.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_abstraction.note:
Enables canopy interception and initial abstraction processes.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_structured_lookup_subgrid.note:
Enables the structured lookup-table subgrid formulation on the regular raster model. It uses level-dependent cell and face properties and cannot be combined with Neal or Voronoi subgrid.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_snow_modeling.note:
Enables precipitation partition, snow storage, melt, sublimation, and compaction using the snow columns of LULC_parameters.xlsx.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_WQ_Rasters.note:
Uses spatial water-quality coefficient rasters B1, B2, W1, and W2 instead of the land-cover table coefficients.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_capillary_rise.note:
Enables capped upward flow from shallow groundwater to the transmission or root zone when storage deficits exist.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_voronoi_subgrid.note:
Enables sub-grid face tables (stage versus flow area, wetted perimeter and conveyance) on the Voronoi mesh. Used only with flag_voronoi = 1; the table path is set in Voronoi_Settings.xlsx.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_voronoi.note:
Runs the model on a prepared Voronoi (unstructured) mesh instead of the raster grid. Mesh options are read from Voronoi_Settings.xlsx.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_deep_aquifer.note:
Enables the deep aquifer: deep_recharge_fraction of the water-table recharge goes to one linear reservoir per subbasin and returns to the surface after deep_aquifer_tau_days. Requires DeepAquiferSubbasins_path and DeepAquiferChannelWeight_path.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_layered_subsurface.note:
Enables the layered subsurface: three soil layers over weathered-rock layers down to bedrock, one water table per cell (Miguez-Macho et al., 2007 rules). Settings are in the Layered Subsurface block of General_Data (D10:F28) and the optional rasters T21:T28. Requires flag_groundwater_modeling = 1.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_feddes.note:
Enables Feddes root-water stress: transpiration from each soil layer is reduced by its suction head. Heads are in the Feddes block of General_Data (D30:F36). Works with the layered and the legacy soil schemes.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.

flag_implicit_water_table_flux.note:
Solves the Darcy flux between the soil and the water table implicitly in the layered subsurface (one linearised backward-Euler step per cell): 1 (default) stays accurate at long time steps when the water table is shallow; 0 uses the explicit flux, which needs short steps there. Used only with flag_layered_subsurface = 1.

Set 0 to disable and 1 to enable unless the flag description specifies another numeric option.
